requirements.evidence: Every contract property and method is present in app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:23-198, and Serve.php:40-104 has selectedQueueId/mode/lastCalledTicketId/notice/callNext. Routes are at routes/web.php:59-60, and all contract lang keys exist in both locales (lang/en/ui.php:110-152, lang/pt_BR/ui.php). rename() re-derives the slug with 'slug: Str::slug($this->renameName)' (Queues.php:147). The toggle uses a confirmation modal, not wire:confirm (queues.blade.php:104-125). Members tabs gate the invite form (members.blade.php:6-20, 71, 96), and both navbar entries are gated (default-page.blade.php:45-52). Two small things: a tampered mode aborts with 422 instead of following the CallMode::from() wording, and the manager check in the access modal uses '\App\Models\UserRole' with strict in_array (queues.blade.php:140). That namespace and cast can't be verified, and no test checks that the manager label renders.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess/CallNextTicket (Queues.php:91,143,173,223; Serve.php:89). The component uses #[Validate] with validateOnly (Queues.php:29,55,87,138), policies for authorization, a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased, and Bulma markup that matches the members page. Deviations: role logic sits in the view via '@php($isManager = in_array($membership->role, ...))' instead of being computed in the component, and 'mode' has no #[Validate] rule (it relies on CallMode::tryFrom, Serve.php:136-139).

security.evidence: Every client id is resolved scoped to the entity: '$this->entity->queues()->findOrFail(...)' in openQueue, startRename, rename, confirmToggle, toggleActive, openAccess and setAccess, plus 'memberships()->findOrFail($membershipId)' (Queues.php:221). Write actions authorize update/manageAccess, and SetQueueAccess/CallNextTicket authorize internally. $entity and lastCalledTicketId are #[Locked]. render() uses find() scoped to the entity, so a foreign accessQueueId discloses nothing (Queues.php:200-218). Rate limiting is per entity and user and counts only successful calls (Serve.php:78-98). All output uses {{ }}. Minor gaps: openQueue and closeAccess/cancel* do not re-authorize (only mount does), and setAccess has no component-level authorize('manageAccess') because it relies on the action.

tests.evidence: QueuesPageTest covers the happy paths, validation (empty name, duplicate slug, rename collision), employee 403 on both the component and the route, the no-per-row-actions markup, foreign-id tampering for every action (ModelNotFoundException plus no state change), accessQueueId disclosure tampering, mid-session demotion → 403, nested-state reset, and pt_BR/navbar. ServePanelTest covers defaults, employee grants, call order, mode filters, the 30-ticket cap, channel translation, inactive/empty/no-selection notices, foreign queue tampering, 403 without a grant, a tampered mode, the locked-property write and rate limiting. Existing member tests were adapted to the tabs, not weakened: they now assert the invite form on the invites tab (MembersTest.php:405-410).

simplicity.evidence: The code is direct, with no new layers. It reuses the actions and policies, and callableQueues() reuses the 'call' policy through $user->can('call', $queue). Small redundancies: the active/inactive tag markup appears twice in queues.blade.php (rows and detail), and the deactivate/reactivate label expression is repeated four times instead of going into a variable or Blade component.

readability.evidence: Methods are small with clear names and short docblocks on the untrusted properties (Queues.php:35-38, Serve.php:37-40). The style matches Members. A few long Blade lines with nested ternaries (queues.blade.php:94, 121), and a fully qualified enum class in a @php directive.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: the two components and views, routes, navbar, lang keys, the members tabs, tests and the CHANGELOG. The extra lang keys (queues_reactivate, serve_rate_limited, serve_mode_*) are used by the new UI. There is no unrelated refactoring.

issues.explanation: Detecting managers with strict in_array against '\App\Models\UserRole' cases depends on an unverified namespace and enum cast, and no test asserts that managers show 'calls without grant' instead of grant buttons.
Role/business logic is computed in the Blade view with @php instead of being prepared in the component (for example, a set of manager membership ids).
openQueue() (and the close/cancel methods) do not call $this->authorize(); they rely on mount and the scoped lookup, while the policy requires authorization inside every public action.
The public 'mode' property has no #[Validate] rule (for example, in:any,priority_only,normal_only); it is checked ad hoc with tryFrom plus abort_if 422.
The deactivate/reactivate label ternary is repeated four times and the status tag markup twice; a local variable or small Blade component would remove the duplication.
The row button's aria-label is only the queue name, so screen readers lose the active/inactive status shown visually.

review.summary: The change adds the Queues management page and the Serve panel as Livewire components that go through the existing domain actions, resolve every client id scoped to the entity, lock server state and rate-limit successful calls. It also splits the members page into tabs and adds navbar links and lang keys in both locales, backed by a thorough test suite with tamper and authorization cases. The remaining issues are small: role logic in the view with an unverified enum reference, missing explicit authorization on openQueue, and 'mode' validated ad hoc. I would approve with nits.
